definition: Multiple AI agents working in parallel or in collaboration to complete a task faster or more robustly than a single agent.
details: A swarm splits work across specialist or duplicate agents, then combines their results — polling several models for consensus, exploring many solution branches at once, or dividing a large job into sub-tasks. The pattern trades compute for coverage and resilience.
story: Think of a chess player who never commits to a move blindly — they consider the board, try an action, watch what changes, and only then decide what is next. The machine stops just answering one question and starts getting a job done, step by step, checking its work along the way. It plans a little, acts a little, looks at the result, and then decides what to do next. The model stops being a one-shot answer machine and becomes a coworker that checks its own work. That loop of reason, act, and observe is Agent Swarms.
